web_blocks.text: Executive Thesis: Monopoly Fundamentals vs. Stage 4 / Stage 1 Basing Tape

web_blocks.html: Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Company (NYSE: TSM) is a COMPOUNDER_PASS (`kpi_health: PASS_WITH_WATCH`) trading at $398.73 as of November 13, 2026 [21]. Over FY2016–FY2025, TSMC grew USD revenue from $29.43B to $122.42B (+35.9% YoY in FY2025). Sales sped up to $46.72B in Q3 2026 (+41.2% YoY), and October 2026 monthly sales jumped +59.7% YoY [1, 5, 6, 20]. Pure-play neutrality and the Open Innovation Platform (OIP) anchor its merchant monopoly in AI and flagship mobile silicon. A 79% <=7nm wafer mix (33% N3, 8% N2) and CoWoS advanced packaging extend that lead [5, 12, 18].

However, price and tape discipline override FOMO. Two technical feeds frame the pullback: our deterministic `facts_US_2026-11-13.json` ledger classifies TSM as Stage 1 (Basing) because $398.73 sits within -1.07% of its 200-DMA ($403.05) and above its $351.19 20D/63D swing low. Meanwhile, our TradingView snapshot (`snapshots_US_2026-11-13.json`) flags STAGE_4 / AVOID_STAGE4_OR_BROKEN because $398.73 trails the 30-week SMA ($420.49) by -5.17% and the 50-day SMA ($430.11) by -7.30% [21]. Both feeds agree TSM is not in a buyable Stage 2 uptrend (`CAP_REJECTED`), with 4H repair unconfirmed (`4H EMA20 $400.29`, volume `0.79x`) [21]. New capital rates WAIT_FOR_SUPPORT (`$369.38–$380.64`). Existing Schwab shares (2.3344 shares, $930.80, 1.05% NAV, -$69.16 unrealized P&L) rate HOLD_WITH_HARD_STOP at $348.00 (below the $351.19 swing low).

web_blocks.text: Single Hinge Claim, Catalyst Calendar & Risk Guardrails

web_blocks.html: Single Hinge Claim: Our thesis hinges on TSMC sustaining >20%–25% AI/HPC revenue growth and >64% gross margins through 2027 without a hyperscaler capex digestion pause as annual capex jumps to $60B–$64B [4, 5]. This claim is falsifiable via Q4 2026 earnings (~January 21, 2027) [24], December/January monthly sales reports, or fab utilization dropping below 75%. Until then, macro rates (US10Y at 5.10% [28]) and S&P 500 breadth (52.6% > 50-DMA, 6 distribution days [28]) drive the tape. Watch whether buyers defend $369.38–$380.64 above our $348.00 hard stop ($32.64 = 1.91x ATR14 room) [21].

Chapters 1–6 build TSMC's price-blind `COMPOUNDER_PASS` foundation. They trace its 1987 pure-play origin, HPC/N3/N2/CoWoS revenue engine, and Gigafab unit economics. They also audit rival yield failures, 2026 KPI trends, and 10-year cash flow forensics. Chapters 7–9 then add the November 13, 2026 market tape ($398.73), Reverse DCF, and peer multiples (UMC, GFS, INTC, ASML). Those chapters close with Stage 4 technical checks, a Bull vs. Bear steelman, and our `WAIT_FOR_SUPPORT` / `HOLD_WITH_HARD_STOP` playbook.

Bottom line for execution: keep 2.3344 TSM shares in Schwab (`1.05%` NAV) with a hard stop at `$348.00`. Do not deploy new capital or open options at `$398.73` (`CAP_REJECTED`). While `options_snapshot.py` mechanically flags a `2027-01-15 $390/$450` Bull Call Spread (`$2,373` = `237.3 bps` NAV, `2.55x` our `$930.80` equity stake), we do not recommend it today: 4H repair is unconfirmed, expiry falls 6 days before Q4'26 earnings, and `$2,373` oversizes a Correction trade. Stalk `$369.38–$380.64` (`3.20:1` asymmetry to `$485.00` base target) or a confirmed Stage 2 reclaim above `$420.49` (using a post-Feb 2027 expiry if trading options). Park any stopped proceeds `100%` in Cash.

Read the full 10-chapter analysis below before placing any order. It covers the primary SEC 20-F filings, CoWoS capacity math, Reverse DCF inputs, peer multiples, and multi-timeframe technical levels.

book_paragraphs: Welcome to this dossier on Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Company, known by its ticker, TSM. To grasp the physical backbone of the AI era, skip software models and cloud providers. Start in Hsinchu, Taiwan, inside the cleanrooms that make nearly every leading-edge GPU, custom AI chip, and flagship phone processor on Earth.

Yet this is not a cheerleading piece. As of November 13, 2026, TSM trades at $398.73, down 18.20% from its 52-week high. Our market-facts ledger labels it Stage 1 Basing (-1.07% vs 200-DMA, above the $351.19 swing low), while TradingView flags Stage 4 (-5.17% below the 30-week SMA). Both agree TSM is not a buyable Stage 2 uptrend. New capital must wait for support at $369.38 to $380.64 or a Stage 2 reclaim above $420.49. Our existing 2.3344 shares hold strictly with a $348.00 hard stop.

Our single hinge claim is clear: TSMC must sustain over 20% to 25% AI and HPC revenue growth with gross margins above 64% through 2027 as capex jumps to $60B–$64B. That claim is testable at Q4 2026 earnings around January 21, 2027, in monthly sales, and in fab utilization above 75%. Great investing means waiting for a rare monopoly to finish its chart repair so the odds tilt your way.

book_subsections.title: At-a-Glance: The Dual Verdict
paragraphs: For fresh capital, the verdict is WAIT_FOR_SUPPORT. Chasing an unconfirmed stock below its 50-day ($430.11) and 30-week ($420.49) moving averages violates basic risk control. Waiting for $369.38–$380.64 against a $348.00 stop ($32.64 = 1.91x ATR14 below $380.64) gives a 3.20-to-1 reward-to-risk ratio toward our $485.00 base target.

For our existing Schwab position of 2.3344 shares—1.05% of our $88,684.68 portfolio—the verdict is HOLD_WITH_HARD_STOP. We do not panic-sell a world-class monopoly 1% below its 200-day moving average, nor do we let a -6.92% unrealized loss turn into a -25% drawdown if $348.00 breaks. We also reject the mechanical 2027-01-15 $390/$450 call spread ($2,373 = 237.3 bps NAV, 2.55x equity) because it expires before earnings and oversizes a Correction trade.

book_subsections.title: What to Watch Next
paragraphs: Watch three signposts over the next 60 days. First, track November, December, and January monthly revenue reports and fab utilization (>75%) to test our >20%–25% AI/HPC growth hinge claim. Second, monitor $369.38–$380.64 against the $348.00 stop (below the $351.19 swing low). Third, listen to Q4 2026 earnings around January 21, 2027 for FY2027 capex and >64% gross margin guidance.

book_subsections.title: The Core Principle: Respect Both the Business and the Tape
paragraphs: One takeaway anchors this entire monograph: great businesses and great entry points are two different things. TSMC is an undisputed industrial masterpiece. Still, at $398.73 in a correction, discipline demands waiting for $369.38–$380.64 while protecting existing shares at $348.00.

paragraphs: With our thesis, numbers, and risk rules defined, let us begin in 1987 Hsinchu. There, Morris Chang's pure-play covenant set one of the greatest industrial compounding stories in motion.
